title: Technology Sector Update for 07/27/2018: FSLR,TEAM,TWTR
text:

GOOG -2.40%
Technology stocks were sharply lower again Friday afternoon, with shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 losing nearly 1.9% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was dropping about 0.7%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- First Solar ( FSLR ) dimmed during Friday trading, falling as much as 11%, after the photovoltaic panels and battery company swung to Q2 net loss of $0.46 per share, reversing a $0.50 per share profit in the year-ago period and missing analyst projections. Net sales dropped to $309 million from last year and missed the $509.2 million Capital IQ mean. First Solar also narrowed its FY18 revenue forecast by $50 million on both sides of its prior outlook to a new range of $2.5 billion to $2.6 billion, straddling the $2.55 billion Street view. Its FY18 earnings guidance also in line.
In other sector news:
+ Atlassian ( TEAM ) jumped almost 15% on Friday, also picking up an $18 increase in its price target to $82 a share at BMO Capital, after the collaboration and productivity software firm beat analyst estimates with its fiscal Q4 financial results and projected Q1 and FY19 outlooks exceeding Wall Street forecasts. Also, Atlassian late Thursday said it has made an undisclosed equity investment in Slack as part of a new strategic partnership that calls on the companies working together to shift users of Atlassian's Stride, HipChat, HipChat Server and Data Center work tools to Slack prior to being discontinued.
- Twitter ( TWTR ) plunged as much as 18% on Friday after the company said the number of monthly active users on the micro-blogging platform fell by 1 million during Q2 from the previous quarter to 335 million, marking 2.8% year-over-year growth, although that also lagged the FactSet consensus expecting a 3.8% increase over year-ago levels to 338.5 million active users each month. Its Q3 outlook also disappointed and combined with the slower-than-expected user growth, upstaged non-GAAP Q2 net income of $0.17 per share and 24% revenue growth to $711 million, both topping the Capital IQ consensus.
